mappings.note: Translation v1 contains the title 'Au maître-chantre. Psaume de David;' which corresponds to OSMAIN v1's first half, but Translation v2 immediately follows with the historical context found in OSMAIN v1's second half. In this specific translation structure, the title is separated into its own verse (v1), while the historical note starts v2. However, looking closely at the content: Translation v1 has 'Au maître-chantre. Psaume de David;' and Translation v2 has 'Lorsque Nathan le prophète...'. OSMAIN v1 combines both: 'Til korlederen. En salme av David. Da profeten Natan kom til ham...'. Therefore, Translation v1 is a **split** of OSMAIN v1.
Translation v2 contains the historical context ('Lorsque Nathan...') which is the second half of OSMAIN v1. Translation v1 took the first half (Title). Together they form OSMAIN v1.
